name: Moonta Bay
reason: Seaside beach town on the Copper Coast, listed by yorkepeninsula.com.au; beach and jetty give a half-hour stop (rule 2) but one source only.
objection: Moonta and Port Hughes already cover this coast; Moonta Bay is a beach suburb of Moonta, so it may be a near-duplicate (rule 3).

name: Port Victoria
reason: Town with a historic 1878 jetty, Port Victoria Maritime Museum and geology trail; named by yorkepeninsula.com.au and southaustralia.com (rules 1, 2).
objection: Wardang Island, its famous shipwreck trail, is closed to visitors (Point Pearce lands), so the town's draw is smaller than it sounds.

name: Maitland
reason: One of the tourism board's seven headline townships (yorkepeninsula.com.au); stone buildings, but no specific sight named by a visitor source.
objection: Inland service town with a hospital; no source says what to see, so a visitor would not go out of the way (rule 2).

name: Yorketown
reason: Inland service town; Small township with no visitor attraction named by a source beyond its listing in the tourism board's township index; rule 1/2 (nothing to see or do named).
objection: The tourism board lists it, and it is a regional hub for the south of the peninsula.

name: Warooka
reason: Small inland town; Small township with no visitor attraction named by a source beyond its listing in the tourism board's township index; rule 1/2 (nothing to see or do named).
objection: Listed on the tourism board's township index and on the road to Innes.

name: Point Turton
reason: Seaside village and beach listed by yorkepeninsula.com.au; a beach stop is rule 2 plausible but only one source.
objection: Holiday village with a caravan park; no source names a specific beach or sight.

name: Corny Point
reason: Remote village with a lighthouse and surf listed by yorkepeninsula.com.au; Wikivoyage names Corny Point lighthouse (link dead).
objection: Lighthouse may be closed or exterior only; the village itself is a few houses.

name: Stenhouse Bay
reason: Village in Dhilba Guuranda-Innes National Park with the visitor centre, jetty, campground and whale-watching cliffs; named by yorkepeninsula.com.au and the parks page (rules 1, 2). Stands in for Stenhouse Bay Jetty (duplicate).
objection: Part of Innes National Park, which may itself be the destination, so it could be a near-duplicate of the park (rule 3).

name: Inneston
reason: Abandoned gypsum township in the park, a named see on the parks.sa.gov.au page (ruins, interpretive signs, heritage cottages); one spot with Inneston Historic Walk (duplicate of this).
objection: Ruins are unstable and walk-through only; could be judged part of the park.

name: Port Clinton
reason: Small coastal township; Small township with no visitor attraction named by a source beyond its listing in the tourism board's township index; rule 1/2 (nothing to see or do named).
objection: Its Wikipedia hits are on the broader Clinton article, so the signal is weak either way.

name: Black Point
reason: Wikivoyage gives Black Point and Pine Point one township section; seaside holiday settlement, beach (rule 1 counted via Wikivoyage/tourism board).
objection: Holiday shacks with no named sight.

name: Pine Point
reason: Duplicate of Black Point: Wikivoyage lists 'Black Point and Pine Point' as one place; Small township with no visitor attraction named by a source beyond its listing in the tourism board's township index; rule 1/2 (nothing to see or do named).
objection: Two distinct settlements 4 km apart.

name: Coobowie
reason: Small coastal township; Small township with no visitor attraction named by a source beyond its listing in the tourism board's township index; rule 1/2 (nothing to see or do named).
objection: Close to Edithburgh, which is kept; may have a coastline walk.

name: Wool Bay
reason: Coastal township with jetty and lime kilns; no visitor source names them as a stop (rule 1, one index listing only).
objection: Lime kilns and jetty are real heritage; a guide could single them out.

name: Port Rickaby
reason: Small township with jetty; Small township with no visitor attraction named by a source beyond its listing in the tourism board's township index; rule 1/2 (nothing to see or do named).
objection: Jetties are a typical stop for anglers.

name: Tickera
reason: Small coastal township; Small township with no visitor attraction named by a source beyond its listing in the tourism board's township index; rule 1/2 (nothing to see or do named).
objection: Beachside village on the Copper Coast.

name: Price
reason: Town beside a working salt works (Wikivoyage mentions it only as an industry); no public access or sight named (rule 2).
objection: Wikivoyage gives Price its own township line.

name: Port Julia
reason: Small coastal township; Small township with no visitor attraction named by a source beyond its listing in the tourism board's township index; rule 1/2 (nothing to see or do named).
objection: Beach holiday village.

name: Balgowan
reason: Small coastal township with jetty; Small township with no visitor attraction named by a source beyond its listing in the tourism board's township index; rule 1/2 (nothing to see or do named).
objection: Jetty is a fishing spot.

name: Port Moorowie
reason: Small coastal township; Small township with no visitor attraction named by a source beyond its listing in the tourism board's township index; rule 1/2 (nothing to see or do named).
objection: Beach access for the south coast.

name: Curramulka
reason: Small inland town; Small township with no visitor attraction named by a source beyond its listing in the tourism board's township index; rule 1/2 (nothing to see or do named).
objection: Has a local museum.

name: Point Pearce
reason: Aboriginal community (Burgiyana) on Point Pearce Aboriginal Lands; not a public visitor attraction and Wardang Island access is prohibited (rule 2).
objection: Narungga culture is a draw for visitors via organised tours.

name: Bute
reason: Inland town; a fauna park is noted but no visitor source describes it (rule 1/2).
objection: Bute Fauna Park is a possible half-hour stop.

name: Paskeville
reason: Inland town best known for the Yorke Peninsula Field Days, an event (rule 4); nothing permanent named.
objection: Field Days is a major event.

name: Ethel Wreck
reason: Remains of the Ethel (1904) on Ethel Beach in the park, named by parks.sa.gov.au ('Visit... the shipwreck of the Ethel') and yorkepeninsula.com.au (rules 1, 2). Ethel Beach is a duplicate of this.
objection: Wreck is largely buried and sometimes just a few ribs; parks page calls it a 'rare look', so visibility varies.

name: Ethel Beach
reason: Duplicate of Ethel Wreck (same place, one spot).
objection: Beach is the access point and the wreck is not always visible.

name: Cape Spencer Lighthouse
reason: Lighthouse and lookout on Cape Spencer in Innes National Park, named by parks.sa.gov.au and yorkepeninsula.com.au (Cape Spencer Lookout); also the park's whale-watching cliff. One spot with Cape Spencer (duplicate).
objection: Lighthouse itself is not open to the public; the draw is the lookout.

name: West Cape Headland Hike
reason: 30-minute 1 km loop to West Cape lighthouse with 360 degree views, named on parks.sa.gov.au and highlighted by rangers (rules 1, 2).
objection: One agency source and a short walk; West Cape picnic area might be a separate duplicate.

name: Stenhouse Bay Lookout Walk
reason: 1 hour 2 km cliff-top loop with views 'among the best in the park' (parks.sa.gov.au); distinct walk from the jetty car park.
objection: Starts at Stenhouse Bay, which is kept, so it may count as part of that spot (rule 3).

name: Inneston Historic Walk
reason: Duplicate of Inneston: the 2 km loop is the way visitors see the township, kept as one spot.
objection: A separate walk as far as the agency is concerned.

name: Thomson-Pfitzner Plaster Trail
reason: 7.6 km 3-hour return hike along the old railway from Inneston to Stenhouse Bay with interpretive signs (parks.sa.gov.au); a real hike.
objection: One source, overlaps Inneston and Stenhouse Bay, and part of Walk the Yorke.

name: Gym Beach Hike
reason: 9.8 km 4-hour return hike over dunes and mallee between Browns Beach and Gym Beach, agency-listed (parks.sa.gov.au).
objection: Long hike with one source, little to see named.

name: Royston Head
reason: Headland lookout, 2-hour 4 km return hike with 'amazing views of the rugged peninsula coast' (parks.sa.gov.au); a headland a guide singles out, second tier but real.
objection: One source only; hike of 2 hours may be seen as part of the park.

name: Pondalowie Bay
reason: Surf beach and campground in the park, named by parks.sa.gov.au and yorkepeninsula.com.au; a beach (and Yorke's best-known surf break) is a standard second-tier keep.
objection: Campground-driven; the beach may not be distinct from the park.

name: Stenhouse Bay Jetty
reason: Duplicate of Stenhouse Bay (jetty is its main feature).
objection: Jetty is a popular dive and fishing site and could stand alone.

name: Investigator Strait Shipwreck Trail
reason: Wikivoyage and parks.sa.gov.au name it: a heritage trail of 10 wreck sites with interpretive signs around the southern coast.
objection: A multi-site trail rather than one place; Ethel Wreck already covers the main stop.

name: Dolphin Beach
reason: Beach within Innes National Park on the road to Royston Head, listed by parks.sa.gov.au; surf and walks.
objection: Only a one-line mention, with no description of what to do.

name: Browns Beach
reason: Beach and trailhead for the Gym Beach hike; parks.sa.gov.au gives it no description of its own.
objection: Beaches in Innes are typical second-tier stops.

name: Cable Bay Beach
reason: Beach and small campground with offshore-island views; a campground listing, no activity named beyond camping.
objection: Beach would be a second-tier keep if a source praised it.

name: Shell Beach (Innes)
reason: Beach and campground; only a camping listing on parks.sa.gov.au, no sight named.
objection: Shell beach is a pleasant sandy spot.

name: Cape Spencer
reason: Duplicate of Cape Spencer Lighthouse (the cape's lookout and lighthouse are one place).
objection: Parks page names it separately for whale watching.

name: Salt Lake Trail
reason: A self-guided driving route, not a place (COVERAGE 'a spot is a place'); no single stop named.
objection: Coloured salt lakes are a photo draw.

name: Yorke Peninsula Art Trail
reason: Multi-site trail of galleries and studios; each is a business or its hours vary, not a place (rule 2/3).
objection: Tourism board promotes it.

name: Southern Yorke Peninsula Water Tower Mural Trail
reason: A route across several towns, not a single place; each mural is a minor stop.
objection: Murals are free and photogenic.

name: Home Grown Trail
reason: Tour of producers and businesses by arrangement (Wikivoyage); an operator-led tour, not a place.
objection: Named by Wikivoyage.

name: Copper Rail Trail
reason: 25 km sealed walking and cycling path between Kadina, Wallaroo and Moonta, named by southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au attraction pages (rules 1, 2).
objection: A linear shared path with little scenery; may be seen as a facility rather than a draw.

name: Edithburgh Mosaic Walking Trail
reason: Fails rule 1/2: Wikivoyage's only mention is a dead link, and a short coastal mosaic walk is a minor local trail with no guide detail.
objection: It is a free all-hours walk named on Wikivoyage, so a second source could make it a small keep.

name: Wheal Hughes Copper Mine
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Moonta and the YP region page both name the underground mine tour (55 m tunnel); a bookable, open visit of an hour or more.
objection: Tour needs booking and one operator; Moonta Mines heritage area already covers the mining theme.

name: Moonta Mines Museum
reason: duplicate of the Moonta Mines State Heritage Area (Wikivoyage lists it as part of that site)
objection: It is the museum visitors go in for; if the heritage area were not listed as a spot, this would stand alone.

name: Moonta Mines Railway
reason: duplicate of the Moonta Mines State Heritage Area (Wikivoyage lists it as part of that site); the railway is also a ride, not a place
objection: Operates only on set days; if the heritage area is dropped it would matter.

name: Hughes Pump House
reason: duplicate of the Moonta Mines State Heritage Area (Wikivoyage lists it as part of that site); Wikivoyage names it as Hughes Engine House inside the area
objection: A distinct engine house, but not a separate half-hour stop from the area.

name: Splash Town
reason: Rule 1-2: southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au both name this free water park at Moonta Bay, a permanent family venue worth an hour.
objection: A council playground-style venue, only useful in summer for families; not a destination in its own right.

name: Victoria Park, Moonta
reason: Fails rule 3: a local park with one tourism-site mention and nothing named to see.
objection: None found; it could host something visitors do but no source says so.

name: Moonta Bay Jetty
reason: Duplicate of Moonta Bay Beach: a jetty at the same shore, a short look; no guide singles it out.
objection: A jetty is a classic fishing and swimming stop on the Peninsula.

name: Moonta Bay Beach
reason: Rule 1-2: yorkepeninsula.com.au lists the beach at the Moonta Bay township; a second-tier beach stop (swim, walk) that guides recommend.
objection: One source, 0 page views; Wallaroo's North Beach and others are similar.

name: Port Hughes Beacon Reserve Lookout
reason: Fails rule 3: a short roadside lookout in a suburb of Moonta; only the regional site names it, with no detail.
objection: Could be a nice sunset view over Spencer Gulf.

name: South Beach, Port Hughes
reason: Fails rule 3: a local settlement beach, one regional-site mention and nothing distinctive named; Moonta Bay Beach covers the same coast.
objection: It is still a swimming beach people use.

name: Port Hughes Jetty
reason: Fails rule 3: a local jetty, short visit, no guide singles it out.
objection: Fishing jetties are core Peninsula activities.

name: Moonta Rainbow and Flower Murals
reason: Fails rule 1-3: one source, a mural trail of small town artworks with no named detail; a minor roadside-type sight.
objection: Mural trails can be a 30-minute walk if the tourism site publishes a map.

name: The Farm Shed Museum and Tourism Centre
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage region page and yorkepeninsula.com.au (entry about $12) name this National Trust museum in Kadina with the stump-jump plough, Matta House and a miniature train; allow an hour or more.
objection: Volunteer-run museum with limited hours and heat closures.

name: Kadina Water Tower Mural
reason: Fails rule 3: a single mural, a minor roadside sight with one mention.
objection: Public art can be a photo stop.

name: Matta House Kadina
reason: duplicate of The Farm Shed Museum and Tourism Centre: Matta House is the mine manager's residence within the museum site (yorkepeninsula.com.au listing).
objection: It has its own tourism listing and Wikipedia article.

name: Wallaroo Heritage and Nautical Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Wallaroo See entry and yorkepeninsula.com.au; a museum open daily 10-4 with ghost tours.
objection: Small local museum; its draw is local history only.

name: Wallaroo Jetty
reason: Fails rule 3: a town jetty, short visit; Wallaroo's other waterfront candidates cover the same place.
objection: The jetty is Wallaroo's main waterfront feature.

name: Wallaroo Marina
reason: Fails rule 2: a marina is a boating facility, not a place to see.
objection: A harbour stroll is possible but no source says so.

name: Office Beach, Wallaroo
reason: Fails rule 3: a minor town beach, one regional-site mention; North Beach is the beach the tourism sites name.
objection: Locals' swimming beach.

name: Sailing Beach, Wallaroo
reason: Fails rule 3: a minor town beach next to the marina, one regional-site mention.
objection: Locals' swimming beach.

name: North Beach, Wallaroo
reason: Rule 1-2: both southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au name North Beach; a long swimming beach with a Wikipedia article.
objection: Another plain town beach.

name: Wallaroo Mines
reason: Case for: a former copper mining area at Kadina that yorkepeninsula.com.au lists, with 1558 page views and heritage ruins. Against: one source, the mining story is told at Moonta Mines and the Farm Shed Museum, and no source says what a visitor can do there.
objection: Could be a free heritage walk, but unverified.

name: Hillside Mine
reason: Fails rule 1-2: no counted source found (Wikipedia only); a former mine site that no visitor source names.
objection: 1414 page views suggest interest, but as a history topic.

name: Copper Coast Putt Putt
reason: Fails rule 2-3: a mini-golf business, not a distinct draw.
objection: A family attraction listed by the tourism site.

name: Wallaroo Skate Park
reason: Fails rule 3: a local skate park, an ordinary suburban facility.
objection: None for a visitor.

name: Map the Miner
reason: outside the region: belongs to the region covering Kapunda (coordinates about -34.35, 138.91), not Yorke Peninsula; no counted source found either.
objection: It is a Big Thing and would be a keep in its own region.

name: Kadina Heritage
reason: duplicate of The Farm Shed Museum and Tourism Centre: the Copper Coast council's Kadina Heritage Museum page describes the same National Trust museum.
objection: If the two were different sites it would be a separate museum.

name: Hillocks Drive Rock Pools
reason: Fails rule 3: a roadside rock-pool stop with one regional-site mention and no guide detail.
objection: Rock pools are a swimmable draw on this coast.

name: Hillocks Ocean Pod
reason: Fails rule 2: accommodation (an operator's pod), not a place to visit.
objection: southaustralia.com features it prominently.

name: Port Broughton Historic Jetty
reason: Fails rule 3: a town jetty; Wikivoyage names it with no detail, a short stop.
objection: Wikivoyage's lead See entry for the town.

name: Port Broughton Heritage Centre and Museum
reason: Case for: Wikivoyage and yorkepeninsula.com.au both name this local history museum ($7 entry). Against: open only Tuesday and Thursday 1-3 pm, small local museum, so hard to arrive whenever.
objection: It is the only See item besides the jetty on Wikivoyage's Port Broughton page.

name: Fisherman Bay
reason: Fails rule 1-2: a small settlement; the single regional-site mention names nothing to see or do.
objection: 1113 page views and a bay on Spencer Gulf could be a stop.

name: Bublacowie Military Museum
reason: Case for: History SA and Weekend Notes describe a private museum with cannon, vehicles and a Storch aircraft, $10 entry. Against: no counted visitor source found, open only some days and closed in July, a small private collection.
objection: The Peninsula has few military sights, but no tourism-board listing was found.

name: Paskeville Field Days
reason: Fails rule 4: a biennial event, not a place.
objection: Wikivoyage covers it as a major regional event, suited to a tip not a spot.

name: Wardang Island
reason: Fails rule 2: part of Point Pearce Aboriginal Lands, access prohibited or by permission only (Visit Yorke Peninsula, SA heritage trail sheet); not open to the public.
objection: Shipwreck heritage trail and 2627 views; permission may be obtainable.

name: Port Victoria Maritime Museum
reason: Case for: yorkepeninsula.com.au names this museum in the old grain-race port. Against: one counted source, small volunteer-run museum, short visit.
objection: Port Victoria has no other indoor sight and Wikipedia has an article.

name: Port Victoria Jetty
reason: Fails rule 3: a historic jetty on the town front; one mention, short visit.
objection: The port's last Grain Race history makes the jetty a trail start.

name: Wardang Island Shipwreck Trail
reason: Fails rule 2: a dive trail around an island with restricted access; duplicate of Wardang Island.
objection: Yorke Peninsula tourism pages promote it for novice divers.

name: Bird Islands Conservation Park
reason: Fails rule 2: offshore bird islands with no visitor facilities; Wikivoyage mentions it only in passing, and no counted source gives a visit.
objection: Wikipedia has 549 views; could be viewed from a boat.

name: Pitts Cutting Lookout
reason: Fails rule 3: a roadside lookout with a single mention and no detail.
objection: Lookouts are on the peninsula's tourist map.

name: Mills Gully Lookout
reason: Fails rule 3: a roadside lookout with a single mention and no detail.
objection: Lookouts are on the peninsula's tourist map.

name: Sincock Square Reserve
reason: Fails rule 3: a small local reserve, nothing to see.
objection: None.

name: Bute Fauna Park
reason: Case for: listed by yorkepeninsula.com.au as a fauna park, animals to see for an hour. Against: one source, small park, unverified whether it is open.
objection: A fauna park would be a family draw in a thin inland area.

name: Port Rickaby Jetty
reason: Fails rule 3: a small jetty at a hamlet; a short stop and one mention.
objection: Jetty fishing is popular.

name: Point Turton Beach
reason: Case for: yorkepeninsula.com.au names Point Turton's beach and the settlement has 2459 views; a second-tier beach stop. Against: one source, a small holiday village, and the beach is not described.
objection: Beaches are named stops, and the Peninsula's southern coast has few listed.

name: Minlaton Harry Butler Red Devil Memorial
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Minlaton See lists the restored Red Devil Bristol monoplane in a town-centre building, free; first over-water flight in the southern hemisphere (history, concrete exhibit).
objection: One counted source, a 15-30 minute stop, and it is a memorial by name; could be a minor memorial or fail as a roadside look.

name: Corny Point Lighthouse
reason: Rule 1/2: yorkepeninsula.com.au names Corny Point (and Wikivoyage mentions the lighthouse, link dead); a lighthouse on a wild south-west coast is a typical second-tier stop.
objection: Only the township appears on the site, not the lighthouse itself; page views 222, the lighthouse is mostly seen from outside; thin evidence.

name: Hardwicke Bay
reason: Rule 1/3: a coastal holiday settlement listed only as a township; no source names anything to see or do beyond the town.
objection: The township page exists on the tourism site and the beach is sandy; but no named draw.

name: Chinamans Hat Island
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source (re-looked at Wikivoyage Yorke pages and parks.sa.gov.au: not named); offshore rock island with no public landing.
objection: Wikipedia has 911 views; but nobody visits it and no visitor source names it.

name: Gleesons Landing
reason: Rule 3: a minor Walk the Yorke access landing; no source describes anything to see or do, no coordinates.
objection: The trail brand is real and the landing is open; but it is part of the Walk the Yorke trail rather than a draw.

name: Point Souttar
reason: Rule 1/3: a coastal locality listed among towns on the tourism site; no source names a thing to see or do.
objection: Could be a quiet beach stop; unsupported.

name: Ardrossan Jetty
reason: Rule 3: a small town jetty, no guide names it as a stop; fishing platform seen in passing (duplicate-quality with a dozen YP jetties).
objection: Historic jetties are a Yorke Peninsula theme (parks.sa.gov.au mentions fishing off historic jetties).

name: Ardrossan Heritage Museum
reason: Rule 1/2: a community heritage museum named on yorkepeninsula.com.au; open to the public.
objection: One source only, 0 views, small-town volunteer museum with limited hours; arguably a local venue.

name: Ardrossan Murals and Mosaics
reason: Rule 3: a set of town murals and mosaics, scattered street art; no guide singles out a place to go, minor.
objection: Mural trails are a recognised small-town attraction and free.

name: Port Vincent Pontoon
reason: Rule 3: a swimming pontoon listed by Wikivoyage with no description; a local swim spot, not a distinct draw.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it as the only See item, so it is a counted source.

name: Port Vincent Putt Putt
reason: Rule 2: a mini golf course is a commercial amusement, not a place a guide singles out.
objection: Family fun listing on the tourism site.

name: Stansbury Museum
reason: Rule 1/2: two counted sources (Wikivoyage See and yorkepeninsula.com.au); a volunteer local museum, open Wed and Sun 2-4pm.
objection: Short opening hours, small museum, local history; not worth a trip.

name: Stansbury Seaside Markets
reason: Rule 4: a periodic seaside market (weekly/seasonal), not a permanent venue.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it under Do.

name: Stansbury Foreshore Murals
reason: Rule 3: foreshore murals, minor public art with no guide naming a stop.
objection: Free and open.

name: Harbour Masters Park Stansbury
reason: Rule 3: a small foreshore park in town; ordinary local park, no source names a thing to do.
objection: Foreshore park may be a nice picnic stop.

name: Stansbury Jetty
reason: Rule 3: a town jetty; no source names anything to see or do beyond fishing; duplicate-quality with other YP jetties.
objection: Jetty fishing is a YP draw.

name: Edithburgh Museum
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Edithburgh See names it (Sat Sun 2-4pm, adults $3); open to the public.
objection: One counted source, small hours, local history museum.

name: Sultana Point
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Edithburgh Do names it as the swimming beach south of town with white sand and the end of the mosaic walking trail; a second-tier beach stop (COVERAGE.md).
objection: Only one counted source and beach is small; page views 242.

name: Edithburgh Tidal Pool
reason: Rule 1/2: two counted sources (Wikivoyage Edithburgh Do and yorkepeninsula.com.au); a tidal sea-water swimming pool set into the cliff, with change rooms, free and always open.
objection: Local swimming pool; a tidal pool is a modest draw, a half hour swim.

name: Edithburgh Jetty
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage names Edithburgh Jetty as a popular scuba and snorkel venue (and in its Yorke regional listing with coordinates).
objection: Divers only in practice; a jetty is not a distinct sight for general visitors; duplicate of other YP jetties.

name: Troubridge Island
reason: Rule 1/2: three counted sources including parks.sa.gov.au (Troubridge Island Conservation Park) and Wikivoyage Edithburgh: the 1855 cast-iron lighthouse and keepers cottage, visited by boat from Edithburgh (island is the spot, not the boat).
objection: Permit and boat access needed; most visitors will not go; seabird sanctuary with restricted access.

name: Troubridge Hill Lighthouse
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source (Wikivoyage only mentions it in passing as a working light, not the island one); a working lighthouse with no named visit.
objection: Lighthouses are a recognised draw; but nothing says it is open.

name: Wool Bay Jetty and Lime Kilns
reason: Rule 1/2: yorkepeninsula.com.au lists Wool Bay as a town; the historic jetty and lime kilns are a free heritage stop on the coast road.
objection: Only the town name is in the source I could open, not the kilns specifically; a ten-minute look.

name: Coobowie Aquatic Reserve
reason: Rule 1: no counted source (re-looked); a marine aquatic reserve with no visitor facility named.
objection: Aquatic reserves can be snorkel spots; nothing says so here.

name: Yorketown Pink Lakes
reason: Rule 1/4: yorkepeninsula.com.au and southaustralia.com use pink salt lakes in their lead copy; Yorketown lakes are a photogenic stop but colour varies by season and the lakes are mostly seen from the road.
objection: Colour is not there whenever you arrive, the entry is a generic group of lakes (duplicate of Salt Lake Trail), no named access point.

name: Wattle Point Wind Farm
reason: Rule 1/2: no counted source; an operating wind farm with no public visitor facility named.
objection: Wind farms are sometimes viewed from the road; nothing says so.

name: Sunny Hill Distillery
reason: Rule 2: a single brewery or distillery operator with no visitor source singling it out as a landmark in its own right.
objection: Southaustralia.com names it, and food and drink is a regional draw.

name: Watsacowie Brewery
reason: Rule 2: a single brewery or distillery operator with no visitor source singling it out as a landmark in its own right.
objection: Southaustralia.com names it, and food and drink is a regional draw.

name: Hedonbar Brewing Company
reason: Rule 2: a single brewery or distillery operator with no visitor source singling it out as a landmark in its own right.
objection: Southaustralia.com names it, and food and drink is a regional draw.

name: Marion Bay Ocean Safari
reason: Operator: a boat tour company; the place it goes to (Innes National Park) is the spot.
objection: Two sources name it.

name: Nharangga Aboriginal Cultural Tours
reason: Operator: a cultural tour operator, not a place; any site it visits is the spot.
objection: Aboriginal cultural experiences are a regional theme.

name: Marion Bay Beach
reason: Rule 1/3: Wikivoyage Marion Bay names the town as the gateway to Innes National Park, not the beach; the park and its beaches are covered separately.
objection: The beach is a real sandy beach with high page views (3151).

name: Leven Beach Conservation Park
reason: Rule 1: no counted source (parks.sa.gov.au regional list names only Innes, Troubridge Island and the marine park; Wikivoyage only lists the park by name): an unvisited conservation park with no visitor facilities.
